title: Split-brain: how it happens, and what fencing costs

videos.script: A cluster manager prevents two primaries, as long as a primary that loses its key notices and stops. Noticing takes a process that is running. {{notice}} You freeze the leader's Patroni and leave its database alone. Another node takes the key, and now two servers take orders. {{two}} Then the frozen process wakes up, rewinds its database into a replica, and an order that was confirmed to a customer is gone. Nothing reports it. {{lost}} Fencing is making sure the old primary has stopped before the new one starts: a watchdog, a power switch, a network cut. {{fence}} And one fence you already have: with a synchronous standby, the old primary cannot confirm a single commit. {{sync}}
